original_question: Let f be a nonzero integrable function on R such that the set {x in R : f(x) != 0} has finite Lebesgue measure. Suppose f tiles R at some level w with a translation set Lambda subset R of bounded density. Must Lambda have a periodic structure, meaning that Lambda can be represented as a disjoint union of finitely many arithmetic progressions of the form a_j Z + b_j with a_j > 0?
target_in_paper: Section 6.2, unnumbered open problem "Non-periodic tilings": whether a nonzero L^1(R) function whose nonzero set has finite measure can tile with a bounded-density translation set only when the translation set has periodic structure. ([eigen-space.org](https://eigen-space.org/mk/ps/ontiling.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's exact formulation: it has the right ambient space R, the right hypothesis f in L^1(R) with f nonzero, the finite-measure condition on {x : f(x) != 0}, the bounded-density assumption on Lambda, and the intended conclusion that Lambda should have periodic structure as a finite disjoint union of arithmetic progressions a_j Z + b_j. ([eigen-space.org](https://eigen-space.org/mk/ps/ontiling.pdf))
missing_details: To make the question fully stand-alone in the paper's sense, define "f tiles R at level w by Lambda" by requiring sum_{lambda in Lambda} f(x-lambda) = w a.e., with absolute convergence of the series a.e., exactly as in (1.1). ([eigen-space.org](https://eigen-space.org/mk/ps/ontiling.pdf))

State explicitly that the translation set Lambda is discrete; this is part of the paper's basic definition of tiling, even though Section 6.2 shortens the wording to "a translation set Lambda of bounded density." ([eigen-space.org](https://eigen-space.org/mk/ps/ontiling.pdf))
Spell out bounded density as sup_{x in R} #(Lambda intersect [x, x+1)) < infinity, matching definition (1.2). ([eigen-space.org](https://eigen-space.org/mk/ps/ontiling.pdf))

Use the paper's exact periodic-structure formulation: Lambda is a disjoint union of finitely many arithmetic progressions a_j Z + b_j with a_j, b_j real and a_j > 0, as in (1.4). ([eigen-space.org](https://eigen-space.org/mk/ps/ontiling.pdf))

For paper-faithful context, note that this open problem is exactly the finite-measure analogue of Theorem 1.5, which proves periodic structure under the stronger compact-support assumption. ([eigen-space.org](https://eigen-space.org/mk/ps/ontiling.pdf))
refined_question: Let f be a nonzero function in L^1(R), and assume that the set {x in R : f(x) != 0} has finite Lebesgue measure. Let Lambda subset R be a discrete set of bounded density, meaning sup_{x in R} #(Lambda intersect [x, x+1)) < infinity. Suppose that for some constant w one has sum_{lambda in Lambda} f(x-lambda) = w for almost every x in R, and that this series converges absolutely almost everywhere. Must Lambda have periodic structure; that is, must there exist N >= 1 and real numbers a_j > 0, b_j (1 <= j <= N) such that Lambda is a disjoint union of the arithmetic progressions a_j Z + b_j? ([eigen-space.org](https://eigen-space.org/mk/ps/ontiling.pdf))
justification: This is the first open problem stated in Section 6.2, not the follow-up weaker special case about indicator functions. Your draft already captures the target almost verbatim. The only paper-critical items that remained implicit were the exact tiling definition from (1.1), the bounded-density definition (1.2), and the formal meaning of periodic structure from (1.4). The surrounding context shows why the question is sharply scoped: Theorem 1.5 proves the same conclusion when f has compact support, while Theorem 1.8 shows that non-periodic tilings with bounded-density translation sets do exist once one allows sufficiently sparse but still unbounded support, so the finite-measure condition is precisely the unresolved boundary case isolated by the paper. ([eigen-space.org](https://eigen-space.org/mk/ps/ontiling.pdf))
